# Educators & Students Explore Musical Possibilities at The NAMM Show​

Events • Jan 26–30, 2027 | Exhibits • Jan 28–30, 2027 | Anaheim Convention Center

*   [Buy a Booth](https://www.namm.org/thenammshow/exhibit/2027#booth)
*   [Attend The NAMM Show](https://www.namm.org/thenammshow/attend)

![Image 26: StudentMeetsStevieWonder_TheNAMMShow](https://www.namm.org/sites/default/files/styles/promo/public/2026-08/StudentMeetsStevieWonder_TheNAMMShow.jpg?itok=74yjD-Bo)

### This Is Where You Connect With a Global Community of Innovators, Musicians, Fellow Students and Educators​

The NAMM Show is the largest annual gathering for the music products industry, uniting all the people who participate in music making. Here you'll connect with music product manufacturers, retailers, artists, creators and pros from across industry segments. Music educators and students are also part of the mix, attending the show to get plugged into the scene and discover the gear and trends shaping music. Held [January 26-30, 2027](https://www.namm.org/attend), at the Anaheim Convention Center in Southern California, this is where you recharge your passion for music through product demos, education sessions and live music showcases over five energizing days. ​

![Image 27: NAMMShowAttendeesDemoPianos](https://www.namm.org/sites/default/files/styles/promo/public/2026-08/NAMMShowAttendeesDemoPianos.JPG?itok=pofN7fto)

### Get Up Close and Personal With the Latest Music Gear and Hundreds of Brands ​

The halls of the Anaheim Convention Center pop with lively musical instrument and technology demos, providing music educators and students the unique opportunity to get hands-on with all kinds of gear. Whether it's a saxophone, flute, piano, marimba, audio production studio or accessory, it's all at The NAMM Show. Product areas include:​

*   Guitars, effects and pedals​
*   Keyboards and synthesizers​
*   Bass, pianos, drums and percussion​
*   Band and orchestra musical instruments​*   Pro audio, live sound and DJ equipment​
*   Software and plug-ins​
*   Live events technology​
*   Folk musical instruments​
*   Print and digital music​

# The NAMM Foundation Supports Research Grant at Drexel University to Examine Effects of Virtual Music Making

Share

Post on Facebook Tweet on Twitter Share on LinkedIn

*   [NAMM Show EPK](https://www.namm.org/epk)
*   [News Releases](https://www.namm.org/news/releases "News Releases")

 Philadelphia, PA 

September 12, 2008

The NAMM Foundation today announced it has awarded a grant to Drexel University, which will be conducting research on how video games that simulate music making, such as _Guitar Hero_ or _Rock Band_, might serve as an inspiration or learning tool for middle-and-high-school students to develop musical skills.

The proposed research will investigate the following questions regarding musical video games:

1.   Does game proficiency have a positive impact on musical skill development?
2.   Does avid game playing lead to the pursuit of other music-making outlets?
3.   Does interest and regular participation in the playing of music video games affect whether a student seeks additional formal music education?

According to principal investigator Youngmoo Kim, assistant professor in the electrical and computer engineering department at Drexel University, video games based on the premise of simulated music play are indicative of a strong demand within society for some form of musical experience and expression.

“In particularly at-risk communities, true music education has been a lesser priority within the public school curriculum and in some areas has disappeared completely,” Kim said. “For students within school districts that provide little or no funding for fine arts programs, music video games may represent the foremost form of musical interaction to which these students are exposed. Consequently, it is crucial to understand the impact and the potential for these music games to serve as a learning tool—ranging from the amount of interest the games generate in making music and pursuing music education, to their impact on actual musical skill development.”

Mary Luehrsen, executive director of The NAMM Foundation, said that the research being conducted at Drexel University supports the overall mission of The NAMM Foundation to encourage more people to get involved in playing music.

“The ‘crossover’ potential of music video games to musical skill development and literacy has not been studied, and this technology has great appeal for all ages,” said Luehrsen. “This study has the potential to reveal important connections between technology and the innate drive to make music.”

# What We Do

## Featured Programs

[![Image 2](https://www.nammfoundation.org/sites/default/files/styles/lennon_3_col__medium_1x/public/files/2024-11/NF_Grantee_PrimaryImage_720x405.jpg?itok=yPeC2D-o)](http://www.nammfoundation.org/global-grantmaking)

## [Global Grantmaking](http://www.nammfoundation.org/global-grantmaking)

Our Global Grantmaking invests in charitable organizations worldwide that demonstrate a significant impact on music career mobility and the creation of more music makers across the lifespan of learning. 

[![Image 3: middle school child learning the uke during NAMM's Day of Service at The 2020 NAMM Show](https://www.nammfoundation.org/sites/default/files/styles/lennon_3_col__medium_1x/public/files/2020-01/DOS_Uke.jpeg?itok=yp-ojpBD)](http://www.nammfoundation.org/projects/namm-foundation-day-service)

## [Day of Service](http://www.nammfoundation.org/projects/namm-foundation-day-service)

The Foundation hosts days of service and learning in Anaheim, CA and Washington DC for NAMM members. These events empower NAMM members to make a positive impact and take volunteerism ideas back to their hometowns and businesses.

[![Image 4: Image of college students that received the 2024 Lamond GenNext Award](https://www.nammfoundation.org/sites/default/files/styles/lennon_3_col__medium_1x/public/files/2024-10/careermobility.jpg?itok=xl_gyEhH)](http://www.nammfoundation.org/projects/careermobility)

## [Career Mobility: Careers in Music, Scholarships, Awards](http://www.nammfoundation.org/projects/careermobility)

Through scholarships, awards, and the Careers in Music initiative, The NAMM Foundation tackles the challenges of career mobility within the music products industry.

[![Image 5: Museum of Making Music](https://www.nammfoundation.org/sites/default/files/styles/lennon_3_col__medium_1x/public/files/2020-02/mommsitplay.jpg?itok=bQCu5-6L)](http://www.nammfoundation.org/projects/museum-making-music)

## [Museum of Making Music](http://www.nammfoundation.org/projects/museum-making-music)

Located at the NAMM headquarters in Carlsbad, CA, the Museum of Making Music celebrates the impact of the music products industry through exhibitions, concerts and educational programs. 

[![Image 6: Image of a girl playing the flute](https://www.nammfoundation.org/sites/default/files/styles/lennon_3_col__medium_1x/public/files/2023-10/BCME_24_720x405.jpg?itok=tqIk-cgP)](http://www.nammfoundation.org/what-we-do/bcme)

## [Best Communities for Music Education](http://www.nammfoundation.org/what-we-do/bcme)

Celebrating schools and districts leading the way in music education and expanding access for all students.

[![Image 7: A classroom visiting the Museum of Making Music](https://www.nammfoundation.org/sites/default/files/styles/lennon_3_col__medium_1x/public/files/2024-09/mmh-photo.jpg?itok=vNig9Hw5)](http://www.nammfoundation.org/music-museum-k12-curriculum)

## [Making Music Happen K-12 Curriculum](http://www.nammfoundation.org/music-museum-k12-curriculum)

In collaboration with the writing team at F-flat Books, the NAMM Museum of Making Music has created a free K-12 curriculum built upon the museum's unique content and resources.

# Artists & The Music Business Converge at The NAMM Show​

Events • Jan 26–30, 2027 | Exhibits • Jan 28–30, 2027 | Anaheim Convention Center

*   [Buy a Booth](https://www.namm.org/thenammshow/exhibit/2027#booth)
*   [Attend The NAMM Show](https://www.namm.org/thenammshow/attend)

![Image 26](https://www.namm.org/sites/default/files/styles/promo/public/2026-07/NS20_17_194057_6452_web.jpg?itok=KrbrPyjH)

### This Is Where the Connection Is Real

​For decades, artists from around the world have been drawn to the energy of The NAMM Show. The world's annual gathering place for the music products industry, The NAMM Show showcases the latest musical instruments, pro audio gear, live event equipment and everything in between that serves the technical and creative needs of the music business. Each January in the halls of the Anaheim Convention Center in Southern California, industry pros get directly connected to brands both well-known and trailblazing, testing the latest products and having conversations that often lead to new collaborations and business opportunities. Find your connection here.

![Image 27](https://www.namm.org/sites/default/files/styles/promo/public/2026-07/NS20_16_134021_0488_web.jpg?itok=RpUmRmvX)

### Discover the Gear and Technology Inspiring the Music Business

Discover solutions that can transform the way you do business in the year ahead. The NAMM Show offers ample demoing opportunities and meeting spaces to connect with your contacts. Product areas include:

*   Guitars, Effects and Pedals​
*   Keyboards and Synthesizers​
*   Bass, Pianos, Drums and Percussion​
*   Band and Orchestra Musical Instruments​*   Pro Audio, Live Sound and DJ Equipment​
*   Software and Plug-Ins​
*   Live Event Technology​
*   Print and Digital Music​
*   Accessories and More

## Industry Insights

 This NAMM U breakfast session kicks off the show, featuring dynamic discussions with industry leaders who share their views on how and why our industry landscape is changing. Hosted by NAMM President and CEO John Mlynczak, don't miss the conversation that addresses how music businesses can continue thriving amid fast change.

## NAMM TEC Awards

 You'll find a packed house at the NAMM Technical Excellence & Creativity Awards, held every year to recognize the most innovative products and people of the pro audio and sound production space. This is a career highlight for professionals and a celebration of successful team collaborations, entwined with star hosts and live performances. 

[Learn More](https://www.tecawards.org/)

![Image 30](https://www.namm.org/sites/default/files/styles/full_content/public/2026-07/NS26_22_231207_1083_web.jpg?itok=jQNGJyYJ)

 Be part of the event that recognizes innovation and iconic artists in the bass world. Back for another year, and this time right on The NAMM Show Campus, the Bass Magazine Awards promises to be a high-energy evening of live performances, special guests and buzz-worthy moments for the bass community.

## She Rocks Awards

### “I'm here to network and meet amazing musicians, learn as much as possible, and experience the show to the fullest. The energy is off the charts.”

Melanie Chryshelle, Jazz Singer

[![Image 33](https://www.namm.org/sites/default/files/styles/promo/public/2026-07/NS26_22_171927_0031_web.jpg?itok=oGtQe6tE)](https://namm26.mapyourshow.com/8_0/sessions/#/)

### [Education Sessions for Artists & Music Business Pros](https://namm26.mapyourshow.com/8_0/sessions/#/)

Find hundreds of education sessions at the show, including dozens tailored for artists and music business professionals. Tap into expert insights at our sessions, panels and workshops, giving you a renewed look at where the music industry is headed: ​

*   NAMM U sessions provide a diverse range of content addressing the music business and its trends, challenges and opportunities. Past topics include How to Tell Your Brand Story on Instagram, Crafting Song Pitches That Get Heard, and New Trends and Tips for Sync Licensing. ​
*   TEC Tracks is where engineers, producers and artists narrow in on trends, innovation, disruption and opportunity within the audio industry. Past topics include Music in Advertising: A Producer's Update; Behind the Hits: Legends of the Studio; and Charlie Puth: Turning Ideas Into Hit Songs.​
*   The [TEC Tracks Studio Summit](https://www.namm.org/blog/namm-show-education-summits#tectracksstudiosummit) is a unique opportunity to access respected names in pro audio and studio operations. Gain a wider and deeper perspective on the strategies and latest concepts shaping today's studio business.​

[See 2026 Schedule](https://namm26.mapyourshow.com/8_0/sessions/#/)

## Bands at NAMM

Bands at NAMM is where you discover globally-known and emerging artists and get plugged into an electric music scene. Over five days, The NAMM Show offers dozens of live music concerts across multiple campus stages, providing you with a prime opportunity to experience artist stage presence, production techniques, sound technology, audience reactions, and all the elements that merge into a memorable show. No doubt you'll be among the music industry trifecta — creatives, fans and business reps — living up a shared experience, starting in the mornings and going well into the nights.

**Faculty Position in Artificial Intelligence, Entertainment, and Human Communication**Artificial intelligence is transforming every aspect of the entertainment ecosystem—from content creation, production, and distribution to audience engagement, accessibility, labor relations, intellectual property, and communication technologies. To engage these developments, the Northwestern School of Communication invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of **Associate or Full Professor in****Artificial Intelligence, Entertainment, and Human Communication**. We seek an innovative scholar, artist, designer, technologist, legal scholar, or interdisciplinary researcher whose work examines the opportunities, challenges, and societal implications of artificial intelligence across creative industries, communication, performance, and human-centered technologies. We welcome applicants whose work explores these developments through artistic practice, scholarly inquiry, policy analysis, technological innovation, or industry engagement. The successful candidate will join a vibrant interdisciplinary community exploring how artificial intelligence is reshaping entertainment, media, performance, communication, and society.  
  
**Areas of Interest****Candidates May Be Working In Areas Such As****AI and Creative Practice**
*    Stage, scenic, costume, lighting, projection, and production design using AI-enhanced tools 
*    Generative AI in theatre, film, television, gaming, music, and immersive experiences 
*    AI-assisted virtual characters and digital performers 
*    Human-AI collaboration in artistic creation and performance 
*    Virtual production, digital environments, and emerging entertainment technologies 
*    AI-assisted storytelling and audience engagement   
  

**AI, Sound, and Music**
*    AI applications in sound design, music production, and audio engineering 
*    Computational approaches to sound analysis and immersive audio 
*    Machine learning and adaptive sound environments 
*    Ethical and artistic implications of AI-generated music and sound 
*    AI voice cloning and digital voice ownership   
  

**AI, Society, Policy, and Law**
*    Intellectual property, copyright, and licensing of AI-generated content 
*    Labor, employment, and workforce implications of AI in creative industries 
*    Entertainment contracts and governance frameworks related to AI 
*    Ethical, regulatory, and societal implications of AI-enabled creative and communication technologies 
*    Design, development, and evaluation of human-centered AI systems that support artists, performers, designers, communicators, and audiences 
*    Role of AI in expanding accessibility, participation, and inclusion within creative and cultural experiences 
*    Frameworks for responsible, equitable, and transparent AI use in entertainment, media, performance, and communication contexts   
  

**AI, Communication Sciences, Audiology, and Speech-Language Pathology**
*    AI systems supporting vocal health for performers 
*    Machine learning approaches to vocal fatigue analysis 
*    Voice synthesis, voice preservation technologies, synthetic speech 
*    Audience perception of synthetic voices 
*    AI auditory technology for entertainment applications   
  

This position reflects SoC’s commitment to advancing research and education at the intersection of AI, creativity, communication, accessibility, and the future of work. This position is 100% in person and located on Northwestern University’s Evanston campus in the greater Chicago area.  
  
**Employment Term:**This is a full-time continuing senior faculty appointment, service of 9 months paid over 12. The hire would be subject to Northwestern’s tenure approval process.  
  
**Salary:** The expected base pay range for this position at the rank of Associate is $125,000-$148,000, at the rank of Full Professor it is $225,000-$250,00, competitive based upon experience.  
  
_Northwestern University has provided a pay range representing its good faith estimate of what the university reasonably expects to pay for the position. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors including (but not limited to) the experience and qualifications of the selected candidate including years since terminal degree, training, and field or discipline; departmental budget availability; internal comparators; and external market pay for comparable jobs._**Preferred Start:**September 1, 2027.  
  
**Closing Date: October 16, 2026.**Review of applications will begin on October 19, 2026.  
  
**Primary Responsibilities**
*    Maintain an active program of research, creative activity, and/or professional practice 
*    Undergraduate and graduate student instruction 
*    Development of innovative curricula 
*    Student mentorship 
*    Collaboration across disciplines 
*    Service to the department, school, university, and profession 
*    Engagement with industry and community partners   
  

**Minimum Qualifications**
*    Terminal degree appropriate to the field and demonstrated expertise in artificial intelligence and its application, impact, governance, or creative use. The candidate’s appointment may be across one or more departments in the School of Communication with the tenure home determined by the major field of expertise.   
  

**Who Should Apply?**
*    We welcome applications from theatre and performance designers, sound designers, communication scientists, audiologists, speech-language pathologists, media scholars, legal scholars, social scientists, and interdisciplinary researchers whose work bridges technology and human creativity.   
  

**Application Documents**Applications will be accepted via Northwestern Careers. For full consideration, please be sure to include the following materials in your application:  
  

*    Cover letter describing relevant interests, preparation, and experience; candidates should specifically address how previous experiences relate to qualifications for the role 
*    Current CV, including links to creative works, if applicable 
*    Three (3) contacts for letters of recommendation, of which at least one should address teaching qualifications   
  

**Forward questions regarding the position to the search chair, Professor Darren Gergle (****dgergle@northwestern.edu****). For more information about the School of Communication, please visit our****website****.****The School**The School of Communication has five departments and offers a suite of interdisciplinary undergraduate, professional, and graduate programs. The departments span the communication arts and sciences including the Department of Radio-Television-Film, the Roxelyn and Richard Pepper Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders, the Department of Communication Studies, the Department of Performance Studies, and the Department of Theatre (which includes music theatre and dance). The school offers instruction to roughly 900 undergraduate majors and 650 graduate and professional students. Founded nearly 150 years ago, the School has been a leader in developing the communication disciplines and professions, and continues to be a center of excellence in the communication arts and sciences. Our current Dean is E. Patrick Johnson.  
  
**The University**Northwestern University is one of the nation’s largest private research universities. Located on the shore of Lake Michigan, the main campus is in Evanston and the medical campus is 12 miles south in downtown Chicago. There is continuing expansion of University facilities and programs, particularly in the sciences and medicine. A variety of cultural, social, and recreational activities abound on and near each campus. We are committed to supporting a strong campus community.  
  
**Benefits**At Northwestern, we are proud to provide meaningful and competitive benefits. The available benefits package for this position will include health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance; paid medical/sick and parental leave; tuition benefits for the employee and dependents; pre-tax and flex spending accounts for commuting and dependent care; generous retirement savings options; and wellness programs. For a comprehensive overview of available benefits, including eligibility details, visit us at Northwestern Benefits to learn more.

[](https://www.linkedin.com/login?emailAddress=&fromSignIn=&session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fin%2Ffelice-fernandez-mba-racs-11a62b51&trk=public_jobs_message-the-recruiter-cta)

**Job Description**Principal Investigator Dr. Volkan Ergin is seeking a Postdoctoral Fellow to join the Ergin Lab in the Department of Otolaryngology at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center.  
  
Effective gene therapies require both efficient delivery vehicles and well-designed therapeutic cargos. The Ergin Lab addresses these challenges by engineering next-generation AAV vectors for targeted gene delivery to cochlear cell populations and developing innovative genetic cargo designs for inherited and acquired forms of hearing loss.  
  
A substantial portion of this role involves hands-on animal research, including mouse models of acquired hearing loss, cochlear microsurgery, therapeutic delivery, and auditory functional testing. The position offers a unique opportunity to gain expertise across multiple disciplines, spanning gene therapy, synthetic biology, high-throughput screenings, and translational therapeutic development.  
  
Dr. Ergin brings experience from both academia and industry, providing valuable mentorship for trainees interested in academic careers, industry positions, or entrepreneurial ventures. Postdoctoral fellows will be encouraged to pursue independent funding opportunities, including NIH K99/R00 awards and other career development mechanisms.  
  
**Primary Duties And Responsibilities**
*   Perform mouse breeding, colony management, husbandry, and experimental planning. 
*   Conduct cochlear surgeries, therapeutic delivery, cochlear dissections, tissue preparation, and phenotypic analyses in adult mice. 
*   Perform cochlear injection techniques in adult mice, including round window membrane (RWM) injection and canalostomy. 
*   Conduct functional hearing testing, including Auditory Brainstem Response (ABR) and Distortion Product Otoacoustic Emissions (DPOAE). 
*   Analyze, interpret, and present experimental findings.   
  

******Qualifications******
*   PhD, MD, MD/PhD, VMD, or equivalent doctoral degree in a relevant field. 
*   Research experience in inner ear biology and hearing research.
*   Experience working with mouse models under IACUC-approved protocols. 
*   Experience performing functional hearing assessments, including ABR and DPOAE. 
*   Hands-on experience with cochlear injection techniques. 
*   Demonstrated ability to design experiments, analyze data, and communicate scientific findings effectively. 
*   Experience with noise-induced, age-related, or ototoxicity-induced hearing loss models is desirable.  
  

Interested candidates should submit:  
  

*   CV
*   A cover letter describing previous research experience, particularly in inner ear research, and outlining long-term career goals

**Job Description**Principal Investigator Dr. Volkan Ergin is seeking a Project Scientist to join the Ergin Lab in the Department of Otolaryngology at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center.  
  
Effective gene therapies require both efficient delivery vehicles and well-designed therapeutic cargos. The Ergin Lab addresses these challenges by engineering next-generation AAV vectors for targeted gene delivery to cochlear cell populations and developing innovative genetic cargo designs for inherited and acquired forms of hearing loss.  
  
A substantial portion of this role involves hands-on animal research, including mouse models of acquired hearing loss, cochlear microsurgery, therapeutic delivery, and auditory functional testing. The position offers a unique opportunity to gain expertise across multiple disciplines, spanning gene therapy, synthetic biology, high-throughput screenings, and translational therapeutic development.  
  
Dr. Ergin brings experience from both academia and industry, providing valuable mentorship for trainees interested in academic careers, industry positions, or entrepreneurial ventures. Postdoctoral fellows will be encouraged to pursue independent funding opportunities, including NIH K99/R00 awards and other career development mechanisms.  
  
**What will you be doing in this role?**The Project Scientist works independently and in cooperation with the Principal Investigator to make significant and creative contributions to a research or creative project in any academic discipline. The Project Scientist may be an ongoing member of a research team or may be employed for a limited period of time to contribute high-level skills to a specific research or creative program. Project Scientists are not required to carry out independent research or to develop an independent research reputation and do not have teaching responsibilities. Ordinarily, the Project Scientist title will carry out research or creative programs as well as administration of day-to-day lab operations with supervision by a member of the Professorial Series.  
  
**Primary Duties & Responsibilities**
*   May assist in preparation of grant proposals, submissions, publications and presentations but is not responsible for generating grant funds.
*   May serve as PI for certain grants as approved by supervising member of the Professorial Series.
*   May participate in publications and presentations as author or co-author.
*   May develop, adapt and implement new research techniques and protocols.
*   Assists in lab experiments.
*   Analyzes, interprets, summarizes and compiles data.
*   May lead or train Staff Research Associates and Research Fellows.
*   Will assist in day-to-day laboratory activities.
*   Experience with mouse breeding, colony management, husbandry, and experimental planning 
*   Appointees on an academic trajectory will be expected to commit a portion of their time to developing an independent range of research.  
  

******Qualifications********Education, Experience & Skills Requirements:**
*   PhD, MD, MD/PhD, VMD, AuD or equivalent doctoral degree.
*   Postdoctoral experience in inner ear research, preferred.
*   Experience performing auditory function tests, including ABR and DPOAE in mice, preferred.
*   Hands-on experience with cochlear injection techniques, preferred.
*   Experience working with mouse models under IACUC-approved protocols, preferred.
*   Experience with acquired hearing loss mouse models is a plus.

## About us

Since its beginning in 1902, Cedars-Sinai has evolved to meet the healthcare needs of one of the most diverse regions in the nation, continually setting new standards for quality and innovation in patient care, research, teaching and community service. Today, Cedars-Sinai is widely known for its national leadership in transforming healthcare for the benefit of patients. Cedars-Sinai receives consistent recognition for our excellence. Our awards include; being named one of America’s Best Hospitals by U.S. News & World Report, receiving the National Research Corporation’s Consumer Choice Award 19 years in a row for providing the highest-quality medical care in Los Angeles, achieving the longest-running Magnet designation for nursing excellence in California, and being recognized as The Advisory Board Company’s 2017 Workplace of the Year, an award Cedars-Sinai has won three years in a row. This annual award recognizes hospitals and health systems nationwide that have outstanding levels of employee engagement. Cedars-Sinai is a leader in the clinical care and research of heart disease, cancer and brain disorders, among other areas. Pioneering research achievements include using cardiac stem cells to repair damaged hearts, developing minimally invasive surgical techniques and discovering new types of drugs to target cancer more precisely. Cedars-Sinai also impacts the future of healthcare through education programs that encompass everything from highly competitive medical residency and fellowship programs to a biomedical science and translational medicine PhD program, advanced training for nurses and educational opportunities for allied health professionals. Most notably, Cedars-Sinai demonstrates a longstanding commitment to strengthening the Los Angeles community through wide-ranging programs that improve the health of its most vulnerable residents.

 The Department of Biology in the College of Arts and Sciences at Texas A&M University (TAMU) invites applications for separate full-time (9-month appointment), tenure-track **Assistant Professor positions**in **the areas of 1) Plant Biology** and 2) **Microbial Evolution**, with an anticipated start date of **Fall 2027**. As part of a major departmental expansion aligned with our **2020–2029 Strategic Plan****,**these searches aim to strengthen research excellence in **broad areas of biology, including microbiology, biological resilience, synthetic biology, evolution, and biological clocks**. We are especially interested in candidates who employ interdisciplinary, collaborative, and innovative approaches to fundamental questions in plant biology or microbial evolution. Successful applicants are expected to develop and sustain an externally funded research program, contribute to undergraduate and graduate education, and engage in departmental and university service. We welcome applicants whose research transcends traditional disciplinary boundaries.  
  
Texas A&M’s research enterprise is internationally recognized for excellence across the life sciences. The Department of Biology (www.bio.tamu.edu) provides a collegial, collaborative research environment that supports large undergraduate and graduate programs and promotes integration of students into active research. Faculty benefit from access to world-class research and teaching infrastructure, competitive startup packages, and participation in several interdisciplinary doctoral programs, including Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, Genetics, Neuroscience, and Molecular and Environmental Plant Sciences. The department also houses the Center for Biological Clocks Research, which supports research in circadian biology.  
  
In support of growth in the biological sciences, major remodeling of teaching space is underway, and architectural design for a new Biology building is in progress to add significant research space for our faculty.  
  
Texas A&M University is located in the Bryan–College Station metro area. This vibrant and fast-growing community combines arts and entertainment, and strong public schools with a high quality of life. Situated in the heart of the Houston–Dallas–Austin triangle, the region offers the amenities of a large metropolitan area while maintaining a welcoming, small-town feel.  
  
Candidates must hold a Ph.D. in Biology or a related discipline and have a strong track record of impactful research.  
  
For full consideration, application materials must include a short cover letter (one page), a curriculum vitae, and a personal statement that includes philosophy and plans for research (maximum three pages), teaching (maximum two pages), service, and contact information for three references. These materials must be submitted online at apply.interfolio.com/189662 . Please ensure all required documents are complete and accurate to facilitate a smooth application process.  
  
Questions about this search may be directed to Dr. Alan Pepper, chair of the search committee, at appepper@bio.tamu.edu.

**Job Description**Principal Investigator Dr. Volkan Ergin is seeking a Project Scientist to join the Ergin Lab in the Department of Otolaryngology at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center.  
  
Effective gene therapies require both efficient delivery vehicles and well-designed therapeutic cargos. The Ergin Lab addresses these challenges by engineering next-generation AAV vectors for targeted gene delivery to cochlear cell populations and developing innovative genetic cargo designs for inherited and acquired forms of hearing loss.  
  
A substantial portion of this role involves hands-on animal research, including mouse models of acquired hearing loss, cochlear microsurgery, therapeutic delivery, and auditory functional testing. The position offers a unique opportunity to gain expertise across multiple disciplines, spanning gene therapy, synthetic biology, high-throughput screenings, and translational therapeutic development.  
  
Dr. Ergin brings experience from both academia and industry, providing valuable mentorship for trainees interested in academic careers, industry positions, or entrepreneurial ventures. Postdoctoral fellows will be encouraged to pursue independent funding opportunities, including NIH K99/R00 awards and other career development mechanisms.  
  
**What will you be doing in this role?**The Project Scientist works independently and in cooperation with the Principal Investigator to make significant and creative contributions to a research or creative project in any academic discipline. The Project Scientist may be an ongoing member of a research team or may be employed for a limited period of time to contribute high-level skills to a specific research or creative program. Project Scientists are not required to carry out independent research or to develop an independent research reputation and do not have teaching responsibilities. Ordinarily, the Project Scientist title will carry out research or creative programs as well as administration of day-to-day lab operations with supervision by a member of the Professorial Series.  
  
**Primary Duties & Responsibilities**
*   May assist in preparation of grant proposals, submissions, publications and presentations but is not responsible for generating grant funds.
*   May serve as PI for certain grants as approved by supervising member of the Professorial Series.
*   May participate in publications and presentations as author or co-author.
*   May develop, adapt and implement new research techniques and protocols.
*   Assists in lab experiments.
*   Analyzes, interprets, summarizes and compiles data.
*   May lead or train Staff Research Associates and Research Fellows.
*   Will assist in day-to-day laboratory activities.
*   Experience with mouse breeding, colony management, husbandry, and experimental planning 
*   Appointees on an academic trajectory will be expected to commit a portion of their time to developing an independent range of research.  
  

******Qualifications********Education, Experience & Skills Requirements:**
*   PhD, MD, MD/PhD, VMD, AuD or equivalent doctoral degree.
*   Postdoctoral experience in inner ear research, preferred.
*   Experience performing auditory function tests, including ABR and DPOAE in mice, preferred.
*   Hands-on experience with cochlear injection techniques, preferred.
*   Experience working with mouse models under IACUC-approved protocols, preferred.
*   Experience with acquired hearing loss mouse models is a plus.

**Job Description**Principal Investigator Dr. Volkan Ergin is seeking a Postdoctoral Fellow to join the Ergin Lab in the Department of Otolaryngology at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center.  
  
Effective gene therapies require both efficient delivery vehicles and well-designed therapeutic cargos. The Ergin Lab addresses these challenges by engineering next-generation AAV vectors for targeted gene delivery to cochlear cell populations and developing innovative genetic cargo designs for inherited and acquired forms of hearing loss.  
  
A substantial portion of this role involves hands-on animal research, including mouse models of acquired hearing loss, cochlear microsurgery, therapeutic delivery, and auditory functional testing. The position offers a unique opportunity to gain expertise across multiple disciplines, spanning gene therapy, synthetic biology, high-throughput screenings, and translational therapeutic development.  
  
Dr. Ergin brings experience from both academia and industry, providing valuable mentorship for trainees interested in academic careers, industry positions, or entrepreneurial ventures. Postdoctoral fellows will be encouraged to pursue independent funding opportunities, including NIH K99/R00 awards and other career development mechanisms.  
  
**Primary Duties And Responsibilities**
*   Perform mouse breeding, colony management, husbandry, and experimental planning. 
*   Conduct cochlear surgeries, therapeutic delivery, cochlear dissections, tissue preparation, and phenotypic analyses in adult mice. 
*   Perform cochlear injection techniques in adult mice, including round window membrane (RWM) injection and canalostomy. 
*   Conduct functional hearing testing, including Auditory Brainstem Response (ABR) and Distortion Product Otoacoustic Emissions (DPOAE). 
*   Analyze, interpret, and present experimental findings.   
  

******Qualifications******
*   PhD, MD, MD/PhD, VMD, or equivalent doctoral degree in a relevant field. 
*   Research experience in inner ear biology and hearing research.
*   Experience working with mouse models under IACUC-approved protocols. 
*   Experience performing functional hearing assessments, including ABR and DPOAE. 
*   Hands-on experience with cochlear injection techniques. 
*   Demonstrated ability to design experiments, analyze data, and communicate scientific findings effectively. 
*   Experience with noise-induced, age-related, or ototoxicity-induced hearing loss models is desirable.  
  

Interested candidates should submit:  
  

*   CV
*   A cover letter describing previous research experience, particularly in inner ear research, and outlining long-term career goals

# Increased Access to and Equity in Music Education

Initiative**Creating Sustainable Arts Programming in America’s Toughest Schools**

Grantee Partner**Lead Guitar**

[Video 1](link_20)

Lead Guitar reaches students who would otherwise never have the opportunity to learn, create and experience the joy of making music.

Lead Guitar builds free guitar ensemble classes in public schools where 80% or more of students are eligible for Free and Reduced Price School Meals. These are schools that lack access to critical resources and opportunities, including arts education. In-school music education inspires students to engage with their school community in new ways, prompts students to examine and expand their personal narratives, and activates growth mindset. Lead Guitar participants experience the joy of music making while developing discipline, self-esteem, and teamwork skills: attributes that help them realize success throughout their lives.

![Image 1](https://lovellfoundation.org/files/2021/05/201610-Chicago-Tech_Lead-Guitar-students1-1024x683.jpg)![Image 2](https://lovellfoundation.org/files/2021/05/201705-Jose-Luis-Puerta-with-Summit-View-Elem-1024x768.jpg)![Image 3](https://lovellfoundation.org/files/2021/05/201905-Hendricks-ES-Adaptive-Curriculum_Brandon-1024x683.jpg)![Image 4](https://lovellfoundation.org/files/2021/05/20190521-BAker-College-Prep-1024x682.jpeg)![Image 5](https://lovellfoundation.org/files/2021/05/20190521-Kacey-Ellis_Doolittle1-1024x683.jpeg)![Image 6](https://lovellfoundation.org/files/2021/05/20200311-Freddy-with-Morgan-Maxwell-LG-Students--1024x683.jpg)![Image 7](https://lovellfoundation.org/files/2021/06/LA-Teachers-Workshop-2019_Denis-Azabagic-1024x768.jpg)![Image 8](https://lovellfoundation.org/files/2021/06/Ingenuity-event-1024x683.jpeg)![Image 9](https://lovellfoundation.org/files/2021/06/Christian5-791x1024.jpg)![Image 10](https://lovellfoundation.org/files/2021/06/Sky-Islands-students-laughing-with-Teacher-Mike-Bagesse-at-the-2019-Tucson-Showcase-1024x683.jpg)
### FY21 Annual Report

![Image 11: Lead Guitar logo](https://lovellfoundation.org/files/2021/05/LG_Logo_Vert_Stack_TAGLINE_for_Lt_Bkgd_RGB.png)

### Grant Purpose

The purpose of this grant is to lay out a vision for Lead Guitar through 2026 with The David and Lura Lovell Foundation as the key strategic partner supporting all aspects of Lead Guitar operations. Foundation funding will leverage other sources and position Lead Guitar for success by providing seed money for new areas of service and initial capital for critical growth projects, such as the completion and dissemination of Lead Guitar Digital.

Interventions like Lead Guitar can create change on a school and community-wide level by curbing the exodus of engaged families, seeding opportunities for networking and community building through neighborhood and family participation in school events, and creating common positive purpose among student participants that carries over into other activities.

The initiative provides broad exposure to arts learning to some of the Nation’s most disenfranchised students. Lead Guitar’s vision is to empower every learner with an instrument that appeals across genes and generations, using music from a broad range of traditions, and differentiated materials like adaptive and Spanish language curricula. Through mentorship, classroom connections with global artists, and university performances, our students develop skills that help them succeed throughout their lives.

### How You Can Help

Volunteer – Lead Guitar is always looking to pinpoint board members who can represent local interests in our regions of operation. While we don’t have other year-round volunteer positions, Lead Guitar has multiple events in every city we serve that require volunteers, with golf tournament fundraisers and student showcase concerts being chief among them.

Airline miles and hotel points – Since Fall 2021, Lead Guitar has programs in all four U.S. time zones. As we grow, travel expenses, particularly airline tickets, will grow in parallel. For example, In fiscal year 2022, Lead Guitar staff will make 18 round-trip flights an an approximate cost of $76,00 and 40 hotel nights at around $4,000.

Auction and raffle items for Lead Guitar’s golf fundraiser help us raise money to be sure, but also make for a more enjoyable experience for the donors and sponsors who are on the course. This is also a great way to promote a business.

[Donate](link_22) — Check our wish list and ways to donate to choose the right option for you.

### Funding

2014-2025**$1,305,177**

### Future Need

Here are three needs that will be increasingly relevant for Lead Guitar over the next five years:

1.   Salaries and wages for Teaching Artist personnel who serve as classroom instructors and mentors, as well as trainers for teachers account for 64% of Lead Guitar’s total expenses. Donations that support Lead Guitar Teaching Artists in the city of your choice will always be the most effective way to underwrite our core mission.
2.   Lead Guitar Digital is our new online platform that will deliver anytime access to Lead Guitar Teaching Artist videos, sheet music, games, lesson plans and more to 30,000 vulnerable students and their teachers over the next five years in areas where we do not have live operations. Investments earmarked for filming, editing, writing and equipment to create the multi-media learning modules will ensure access to quality music learning in schools that are otherwise arts deserts.
3.   Lead Guitar’s adaptive method – Lead Guitar with Chord Buddy featured in the above video – allows students of all abilities to participate in guitar class and is ready to grow. Investments earmarked for the Chord Buddy adaptive devices, program support and training will help us help schools meet the wide-spread need for music and growth opportunities for Exceptional Education students in under-supported public schools. One program for one school year that serves 15-40 students costs Lead Guitar approximately $8,400 including assistive devices.

Title: Here’s How 3 People Turned Wonder Into Discovery and Change

URL Source: https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/index.html

Markdown Content:
![Image 1](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/x-close.svg)

[![Image 2](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/usnews-logo-B1eZVQoFjW-4.svg)](https://www.usnews.com/ [link_1])

ad content by [**_University of Arizona_**](link_2)

![Image 3](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/info-39D95CF5-FBF4-49D2-91E4-4A2F06433F-Bklee4XqLG.svg)

[![Image 4](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/1EarthSunSet.jpg)](https://www.arizona.edu/ [link_2])

“What difference can I make in the world?” Since 1885, the [University of Arizona](link_2) has helped its students and faculty find the answer through contributions to world-changing research, connections with peer and faculty mentors and development of new community ties.  
‍  
While this incubator for wonder lies in the Sonoran Desert, the University of Arizona’s reach extends far beyond. The school’s faculty translate their imagination and curiosity into academic breakthroughs across the globe … and even into space.  

[![Image 5](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/VideoPlaceHolder.jpg)![Image 6](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Satillet.jpg)](https://www.as.arizona.edu/ [link_3])

# Where Did We Come From?

Wonder

**and space exploration**

That’s a question Chris Walker, Ph.D., is currently searching the galaxy to answer, aided by University of Arizona facilities and expert personnel. In 2017, NASA selected the professor of astronomy in the university’s [Steward Observatory](link_3) as the principal investigator to help map the galaxy.

[Learn More](link_3)

[![Image 7](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/GustoLaunch.jpg)](https://www.as.arizona.edu/ [link_3])[![Image 8](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/GustoBeingBuilt.jpg)](https://www.as.arizona.edu/ [link_3])[![Image 9](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/GustoSpace.jpg)](https://www.as.arizona.edu/ [link_3])[![Image 10](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/ChrisWalker.jpg)](https://www.as.arizona.edu/ [link_3])[![Image 11](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Quote1.png)](https://www.as.arizona.edu/ [link_3])[![Image 12](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Stewart-Observatory-telescope_still-image_20192.jpg)](https://www.as.arizona.edu/ [link_3])[![Image 13](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Satillet.jpg)](https://www.as.arizona.edu/ [link_3])
The $40 million NASA project, the Galactic/Extragalactic ULDB Spectroscopic Terahertz Observatory, or GUSTO, will look at that cosmic gas and dust suspended among the stars of the Milky Way and the Large Magellanic Cloud.  
‍  
“Where we came from was gas and dust, called interstellar medium,” Walker says. “GUSTO looks at three very important atoms for [the] formation of planets and life — carbon, oxygen and nitrogen.”  
‍  
In 2021, Walker’s team will deploy a high-altitude balloon carrying a telescope with carbon, oxygen and nitrogen emission line detectors. The balloon allows researchers to efficiently create a road map of the universe, and in trial runs, “we had more data on a carbon line in one hour than a previous billion-dollar space mission captured in its whole lifetime,” he says. “We were able to demonstrate economy _and_ scientific payoff.”  
‍  
UArizona has a long history of space innovation. “Our scientists built instruments for Hubble; we have telescopes set up on local mountains and instruments in Antarctica,” Walker says. GUSTO’s mission will give researchers a clearer picture of stellar evolution, while helping unravel the galaxy’s complexities and determine where we came from.

![Image 14](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Quote1.png)

[![Image 15](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/CurvedArches.jpg)](https://cfa.arizona.edu/ [link_4])[![Image 16](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Quote2.png)](https://cfa.arizona.edu/ [link_4])[![Image 17](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Wildcat-Statue.jpg)](https://cfa.arizona.edu/ [link_4])

![Image 18](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/ArtHeader.jpg)
If you’ve ever been moved by music, a play or a painting, then you know art’s transformative power. It’s something that Brad Richter, director of outreach for the [University of Arizona College of Fine Arts](link_4) and co-founder of the music education organization Lead Guitar, explores through a program he helped develop, [Arizona Art in Schools](link_5) (AZAiS).  
‍  
In the late 1990s, Richter visited the Navajo Nation in northeastern Arizona, and saw an opportunity to expand the music education curriculum. To help, he founded Lead Guitar, a nonprofit offering music resources in public schools with low access to the arts. In 2013, Richter teamed up with the university to create a similar program using music and dance to help empower middle and high school students. “With AZAiS, we wanted to provide the highest quality arts education possible to families who could typically least afford it,” he says.  
‍  
Thanks to the combined efforts of Lead Guitar and AZAiS, more than 5000 students in 83 schools in Arizona and beyond have access to music and arts education this year alone. AZAiS pairs a university instructor with a certified co-teacher at the school to ensure sustainability. It also brings global artist performances into the schools and AZAiS students onto campus to perform.  
‍  
In addition to tangibly better student outcomes in terms of dropout rates, behavioral issues and academic achievement, “these programs are a connecting point to broader cognitive and well-being benefits — from listening skills to growth mindsets to self-esteem,” Richter says. “Access to the arts allows these students to rewrite their personal narratives.”  
‍  
[LEARN MORE](link_5)

[![Image 19](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/CurvedArches.jpg)](https://ad.doubleclick.net/ddm/trackclk/N510001.4377USNEWS.COM/B23261578.260083363;dc_trk_aid=455781098;dc_trk_cid=123281206;dc_lat=;dc_rdid=;tag_for_child_directed_treatment=;tfua= [link_6])[![Image 20](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Quote2.png)](https://ad.doubleclick.net/ddm/trackclk/N510001.4377USNEWS.COM/B23261578.260083363;dc_trk_aid=455781098;dc_trk_cid=123281206;dc_lat=;dc_rdid=;tag_for_child_directed_treatment=;tfua= [link_6])[![Image 21](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Wildcat-Statue.jpg)](https://ad.doubleclick.net/ddm/trackclk/N510001.4377USNEWS.COM/B23261578.260083363;dc_trk_aid=455781098;dc_trk_cid=123281206;dc_lat=;dc_rdid=;tag_for_child_directed_treatment=;tfua= [link_6])

[![Image 22](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/ArtStudent.jpg)![Image 23](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/ScientistArchLight.jpg)![Image 24](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/ScieneArchHorizontal.jpg)](https://cfa.arizona.edu/ [link_4])

[![Image 25](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/RedBastetball.jpg)![Image 26](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/11image.jpg)](https://drc.arizona.edu/athletics [link_7])

![Image 27](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Bodieshader.jpg)
A lot, if you ask Jenn Poist. Each day, the University of Arizona women’s wheelchair basketball head coach heads to campus at 6:30 a.m. for two-hour basketball practice.  
‍  
[Adaptive Athletics](link_7) at Arizona is the largest collegiate-based program in the United States, providing disability resources to athletes across a variety of sports, including basketball, track, rugby, tennis and golf. Students have access to a specially outfitted fitness center, wheelchair maintenance, training and academic workshops. And in the program’s 44-year history, 34 athletes, including Poist, have competed in Paralympics sports.

[![Image 28](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Quote3.png)](https://drc.arizona.edu/athletics [link_7])[![Image 29](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/BBall_1.jpg)](https://drc.arizona.edu/athletics [link_7])
After losing her mobility at age 7, Poist discovered wheelchair basketball in high school. It was there she was recruited to the university. "I played for nine years as part of the team,” Poist says. “In 2012, I made my first Paralympic team.”  
‍  
She went on to compete in the 2012 London games and won the gold medal in 2016 in Rio de Janeiro. “Before I played basketball, I was struggling with being disabled,” Poist says. “The Adaptive Athletics program gave me the opportunity to go to school while playing sports and doing what I love. It also made me realize that life goes on and there are other people just like me living and pursuing their dreams.[](link_8)

[![Image 30](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Bball_4.jpg)](https://drc.arizona.edu/athletics [link_7])[![Image 31](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/Bball_5.jpg)](https://drc.arizona.edu/athletics [link_7])
‍**“**Being an athlete pushes you to always do better and be better. That spills over off the court, too,” she says.  
‍  
Whether it’s breaking the confines of a wheelchair or breaking into the secrets of the universe, the University of Arizona continues to push the boundaries of possibility with an array of programs and initiatives in the arts, sciences and athletics. Using wonder as a driving force for exploration, discovery and change, University of Arizona students and faculty continue to transform and expand our understanding of the human experience.   
[LEARN MORE](link_7)

[![Image 32](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/CTAGraphic.jpg)](https://www.arizona.edu/ [link_2])[![Image 33: University of Dayton](https://usnewsbrandfuse.com/University-of-Arizona/From-Wonder-to-Discovery-to-Change/images/LogoUA.png)](https://www.arizona.edu/ [link_2])

# UA Program Brings Music and Dance Education to Schools in Need

 By Alexis Blue, University Communications 

June 5, 2019

![Image 3: twitter sharing button](https://platform-cdn.sharethis.com/img/twitter.svg)Post

![Image 4: email sharing button](https://platform-cdn.sharethis.com/img/email.svg)Email

![Image 5: print sharing button](https://platform-cdn.sharethis.com/img/print.svg)Print

![Image 6: facebook sharing button](https://platform-cdn.sharethis.com/img/facebook.svg)Share

![Image 7: linkedin sharing button](https://platform-cdn.sharethis.com/img/linkedin.svg)Share

![Image 8: sharethis sharing button](https://platform-cdn.sharethis.com/img/sharethis.svg)Share

Image

![Image 9: Pablo Esteban Quiñonez Paz learned to play guitar through Lead Guitar, part of the UA CFA in Schools outreach program. He plans to pursue a degree in music at the UA.  ](https://cdn.uanews.arizona.edu/s3fs-public/styles/az_large/public/story-images/pablo.jpg.webp?VersionId=5TY8EDAEIvvlSBSf5qHWOFs0LR.okx0e&itok=z5W9m7MU)

Pablo Esteban Quiñonez Paz learned to play guitar through Lead Guitar, part of the UA CFA in Schools outreach program. He plans to pursue a degree in music at the UA.

(Photo: Bob Demers/UANews)

When Pablo Esteban Quiñonez Paz was a young boy, he listened to his father and brother play "Spanish Ballad" on the guitar and told himself that he, too, would one day learn to play the song.

Fast forward to 2014, when he and his family immigrated to the U.S. from Hermosillo, Sonora, Mexico. Quiñonez Paz was 14 years old and adapting to an entirely new culture and way of life when he set foot in his first guitar class at Amphitheater High School in Tucson.

Now an 18-year-old recent graduate of the school, he's able to play "Spanish Ballad" and a host of other tunes, including the Eagles classic "Hotel California," which he and his classmates plucked their way through during a recent spring morning rehearsal.

Quiñonez Paz is one of 16,500 young students who has benefited from arts education offered through the University of Arizona [CFA in Schools](link_42) program, which works with 75 partner schools in Arizona and across the country to provide music and dance instruction.

Based in the UA [College of Fine Arts](link_43), CFA in Schools deploys experts to help establish music and dance programs in schools that might not be able to offer such programs on their own, either due to lack of resources or cuts to arts funding.

Those experts spend two to three years training and mentoring teachers, who may or may not have experience teaching arts disciplines. The idea is that they can eventually sustain the classes on their own. In Arizona, the trainers are usually UA alumni, students or faculty members.

"The goal for CFA in Schools is to get the highest quality arts education in the hands of the students who could typically least afford it," said **Brad Richter**, director of arts outreach in the UA College of Fine Arts. "We search for schools that have 80% or more of their students eligible for free and reduced lunch, and we offer free programs to those schools."

CFA in Schools has three offerings for middle and high school students: Lead Guitar for aspiring guitarists, UpBeat for drummers, and Step Up for dance. There is also a general music program called Music First for students in kindergarten through second grade.

Richter started the Lead Guitar program independently in 1999 while working as a professional musician. After playing a concert in northern Arizona, he was asked to visit Page High School to teach a guitar workshop. There, he was inspired by a group of students who had begun learning guitar on their own, without any formal instruction. Richter wrote a guitar curriculum for the school's choir teacher so she could help the students continue learning.

The program grew from there, with Richter and colleague Marc Sandroff eventually establishing Lead Guitar as a 501c3 nonprofit organization in 2007. Six years later, in 2013, Richter joined the UA and brought the program with him.

With the encouragement of **Jory Hancock**, director of the UA [School of Dance](link_44) and then-dean of the College of Fine Arts, Richter began using the Lead Guitar model to develop similar programs in different arts disciplines. And so CFA in Schools was born.

Since 2013, CFA in Schools has grown from 17 to 75 schools, including several locations across Arizona, as well as in Chicago, Los Angeles, Colorado and Oklahoma. Lead Guitar remains the program's most popular offering.

Schools chosen to partner with CFA in Schools are typically located in areas where there is strong university partner from which to draw expertise and arts enrichment opportunities.

In addition to its instructional component, CFA in Schools brings students to universities to see performances and to perform in their own showcase concert at the end of the school year.

The program also helps arrange school visits from professional performance artists. In Tucson, for example, world-class artists on the UA Presents season schedule are sometimes brought in to perform for the students at their schools.

"There are three important legs to what we do: the in-school instruction from university-level instructors, training the co-teachers to be able to eventually teach the class on their own, and community and university experiences that get the kids out of school and onto campus," Richter said. "We want them to feel comfortable here and to be celebrated here and to get used to the idea that a university is a place that they're welcome."

The program also serves as a good training ground for university students who are preparing for careers in arts education.

**Steven Lerman**, who is finishing a doctorate in classical guitar performance in the UA [Fred Fox School of Music](link_45), teaches guitar alongside the music instructor at Amphitheater High School. Quiñonez Paz was among his students.

Lerman has been involved with Lead Guitar since he was a UA senior, and he says it's helped him hone his skills as both a teacher and performer.

"It's really fulfilled me with my studies to take what I've learned and help other kids learn and experience something different – something they wouldn’t have had the opportunity, maybe, to do," he said. "As a teacher, it's been amazing to get all that extra experience and to work under different conditions and have to be able to respond to things, but the best part about it has been to just work with the kids."

The intention of CFA in Schools is not to cultivate the next generation of professional musicians, but to give young people – many of whom may come from difficult circumstances – the confidence to pursue whatever they want to do next, said **Holly Holmes**, assistant to the director of CFA in Schools.

"The goal is not to bring up students who are all going to major in the arts, necessarily, but to have that as part of their critical thinking," Holmes said. "It's not about becoming a spectacular performer, but about realizing their potential."

For some, though, a career in the arts does become the ultimate goal.

Now that Quiñonez Paz has graduated from high school, he plans to attend the UA and double major in music theory and guitar performance. He wants to continue performing, with the support of his family and friends.

"It's nice to show the people what you can do," he said, "and that you can become something bigger."
